what: Live updates (OTA, over the air) let an installed Capacitor or Ionic app download a new web bundle (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) without going through app-store review. They only work for changes compatible with the installed native binary, so each bundle should be gated by a minimum native version.
like: Like swapping the pages inside a book cover: you can change the pages anytime, but if the new pages need a bigger cover you must print a new book.
why: Ship a bug fix to users in minutes, not days of store review
Roll out gradually and roll back fast if it goes wrong
Keep one web code line across many native versions safely

steps.d: Live updates cover binary-compatible changes: HTML, CSS, JavaScript and assets.
Channels give separate tracks (dev, staging, production, QA). A channel can be paused, and devices can be routed to a build.
Restrict each bundle to compatible native app versions. Adding a plugin or changing native dependencies needs a new store release first.
The app SDK checks for a bundle, downloads it, then applies it on next start or via a reload call.
Stage the release (for example 10, 25, 50, then 100 percent) and watch errors.
If the app fails to launch after an update it reverts to the last good bundle, and you can also roll back from console, CLI or API.

choices.d: Appflow is closing at the end of 2027 and is not sold to new customers; alternatives such as Capawesome Cloud and Capgo offer channels and rollback. Check current pricing and features yourself.

choices.t: What may go over the air
choices.d: Only web-layer changes. Anything touching native code, plugins or project files goes through the stores.
Tag every bundle with the minimum native version it needs so older binaries never receive an incompatible bundle.
Google Play bans downloading executable code except code run in an interpreter or VM such as JavaScript in a WebView; keep updates to the web layer and check Apple's current rules.

instead.why: To switch behaviour inside an already shipped bundle without a new download
On the web, a service worker updates assets; on mobile this is the store-free equivalent

breaks.t: Bundle needs a newer native plugin
breaks.d: A web bundle calls a plugin the installed binary does not have.
breaks.see: Crashes or missing features on older app versions
breaks.fix: Gate by minimum native version and ship the binary first
Gradual rollout, a channel for QA, and automatic rollback on launch failure
Code-sign bundles so devices install only what you publish

say: I use live updates only for binary-compatible web changes, and gate each bundle with a minimum native version.
I release through channels with a gradual rollout and automatic rollback, and sign the bundles.
Anything that adds or changes a native plugin goes through the stores first; I would pick a maintained service because Appflow shuts down at the end of 2027.

followups.q: Is this allowed by the app stores?
followups.a: Google Play exempts code that runs in an interpreter or VM, such as JavaScript in a WebView. Keep to web-layer changes and re-read current Apple and Google rules.

followups.q: How do you avoid breaking old app versions?
followups.a: Tag bundles with the minimum native version, and keep web code backward compatible for versions still in the field.

today: With Appflow closing on 31 Dec 2027, teams are moving to services such as Capawesome Cloud and Capgo that provide channels, gradual rollout, signing and automatic rollback for Capacitor apps.

check.q: What can a live update change?
check.a: Web layer: HTML, CSS, JavaScript, assets
check.why: Native changes need a store release.

check.q: How do you stop an old binary getting an incompatible bundle?
check.a: Gate bundles by minimum native version
d: Use the same channel for everyone
check.why: Version gating keeps compatible bundles with compatible binaries.

check.q: A bundle crashes on launch. What should happen?
check.a: Revert to the last good bundle
check.why: Automatic rollback restores the previous bundle and stops retrying the broken one.
